meta.title: Directive 2010/64/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 October 2010 on the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down rules concerning the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
Due to the nature of this provision, which sets out the subject matter of the Directive in general terms, implementation was not considered necessary by the Dutch legislator.


As a general preliminary remark, please note that the Directive has been implemented into Dutch law through the Act of 28 February 2013 on the implementation of Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 October 2010 on the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings, Staatsblad 2013, 85 (entry into force 1 October 2013). The full title in Dutch of this implementing Act is Wet van 28 februari 2013 tot implementatie van richtlijn nr. 2010/64/EU van het Europees Parlement en de Raad van 20 oktober 2010 betreffende het recht op vertolking en vertaling in strafprocedures (PbEU L 280). The underlying parliamentary dossier is numbered 33355 and publicly available on zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl.

In this Transposition Table references will be made only to the consolidated versions of applicable laws.


As a further preliminary remark, note that the term 'suspect' in this table may refer to the suspect or the accused, or both, depending on the context. This corresponds to the Dutch legal terminology, in which persons suspected of a crime are called 'suspects', both before and after indictment.

items.text: 2. The right referred to in paragraph 1 shall apply to persons from the time that they are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State, by official notification or otherwise, that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether they have committed the offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

provisions.comment: Article 23(4) refers to the power of summoning an interpreter (if necessary, forcibly) before the Trial Court. By virtue of this reference, the power of summoning an interpreter can be exerted by the public prosecutor during the investivatige phase.
provisions.textEn: If the suspect has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language, the assistance of an interpreter shall be sought. The public prosecutor shall call in the interpreter. Article 276(3) shall apply mutatis mutandis.
In all cases where a suspect who does not speak the Dutch language or has insufficient command thereof is heard, the assistance of an interpreter shall be sought.

The interpreter shall be called upon by the officer conducting the questioning, unless otherwise provided by law. During the investigation, the interpreter may be called upon orally. In all other cases, the call shall be in writing.

items.comment: According to the explanatory memorandum, the legislator takes the view that, in view of its wording, the directive has a more limited effect than Article 6(3)(c) ECHR. According to the legislator, this means that the directive only applies to criminal proceedings and not also, for example, to administrative fines. By contrast, the Supreme Court seems to take as a starting point that the guarantees to which the accused is entitled as such must also be observed when investigators use their powers of administrative control (e.g. custom inspection, see HR 20 February 2018, ECLI:NL:HR:2018:247)

items.text: 3. Where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction regarding minor offences by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed to such a court, this Directive shall apply only to the proceedings before that court following such an appeal.

provisions.comment: Significantly the final wording of the implementing law reflects opinions expressed by the relevant stakeholders (inter alia, Dutch Council for the Judiciary, the Dutch Bar Association) thus leading to the inclusion of this provision.
provisions.textEn: If it appears that the accused has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language and the penal order has been issued because of a crime [not a minor offence], such order, or at least the parts of it referred to in paragraph 6, shall be translated into a language the accused understands. The suspect who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language may request that the penal order be translated into a language that he understands.

provisions.comment: Article 257f, third paragraph, provides that the hearing of an opposition against a penal order takes place in accordance with the sixth, seventh and eighth titles of the Second Book of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Since Title VI contains, inter alia, the provisions on interpretation during the hearing, it is ensured that the accused who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language will be assisted by an interpreter in dealing with his opposition.
provisions.textEn: The case shall be heard in accordance with Part Six, Seven or Eight of Book Two and the description of the conduct in the notice shall be regarded as the indictment. Said description shall be equivalent to the brief description of the conduct in the penal order or shall be a statement of the same offence which meets the requirements of Article 261(1) and (2). In derogation to that extent from Article 349(1), the notice may be declared null and void.

The penal order shall be in writing and shall state: 

a. the name and the known address of the suspect; 

b. a statement of the offence as referred to in section 261(1) and (2), or a brief description of the conduct for which this punishment order was issued, and the time at which and the place where this conduct took place; 

c. the criminal offence that this conduct constitutes; 

d. the punishments, measures and instructions imposed; 

e. the day on which it was issued; 

f. the manner in which an objection may be filed; 

g. the manner of execution.
If a suspect, witness or expert does not know the Dutch language or does not know it sufficiently, the examining magistrate may summon an interpreter

If a suspect or witness cannot hear or speak or only very poorly, the examining magistrate shall determine that the assistance of an appropriate person as an interpreter shall be called or that the questions or answers shall be in writing.

If the interpreter is not a sworn interpreter within the meaning of the Sworn Interpreters and Translators Act, the examining magistrate shall swear the interpreter to perform his duties to the best of his knowledge before the interpreter commences his work.

items.comment: The implementing provisions go beyond what is required by the Directive, in that they provide for the translation of the essential elements of a penal order handed down by the police or prosecutor (and other investigating authorities).

items.text: 4. This Directive does not affect national law concerning the presence of legal counsel during any stage of the criminal proceedings, nor does it affect national law concerning the right of access of a suspected or accused person to documents in criminal proceedings.
items.comment: Due to the nature of this provision, which sets out the subject matter of the Directive in general terms, implementation was not considered necessary by the Dutch legislator.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not speak or understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are provided, without delay, with interpretation during criminal proceedings before investigative and judicial authorities, including during police questioning, all court hearings and any necessary interim hearings.

provisions.textEn: If the suspect has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language, the assistance of an interpreter shall be sought. The public prosecutor shall call in the interpreter. Article 276(3) shall apply mutatis mutandis.

If the interpreter is not a sworn interpreter within the meaning of the Sworn Interpreters and Translators Act [Wet beëdigde tolken en vertalers], the presiding judge shall put the interpreter under an oath to perform his duties in good conscience, prior to the interpreter undertaking his duties.
In all cases where a suspect who does not speak the Dutch language or has insufficient command thereof is heard, the assistance of an interpreter shall be sought.

The interpreter shall be called upon by the officer conducting the questioning, unless otherwise provided by law. During the investigation, the interpreter may be called upon orally. In all other cases, the call shall be in writing.
The assistance of an interpreter shall be reported in the official record.
If a suspect, witness or expert does not know the Dutch language or does not know it sufficiently, the examining magistrate may summon an interpreter

If a suspect or witness cannot hear or speak or only very poorly, the examining magistrate shall determine that the assistance of an appropriate person as an interpreter shall be called or that the questions or answers shall be in writing

If the interpreter is not a sworn interpreter within the meaning of the Sworn Interpreters and Translators Act, the examining magistrate shall swear the interpreter to perform his duties to the best of his knowledge before the interpreter commences his work
If a defendant is not or is not sufficiently fluent in the Dutch language, the hearing shall not be continued without the assistance of an interpreter
In cases where the assistance of an interpreter is requested, that which has been said or read out and has not been interpreted for the defendant shall not be taken into account to his detriment.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that, where necessary for the purpose of safeguarding the fairness of the proceedings, interpretation is available for communication between suspected or accused persons and their legal counsel in direct connection with any questioning or hearing during the proceedings or with the lodging of an appeal or other procedural applications.

provisions.comment: This is a supplementary provision allowing the suspect or defendant himself/herself to ask for the summon of an interpreter, in all cases where the other provisions - obliging the government to provide such assistance. The explanatory memorandum mentions as an example the case of an accused who, while mastering the Dutch language, wishes to attend an interrogation of a witness or expert at the examining magistrate's office, and therefore requests to be accompanied by an interpreter to interpret the interrogation.
provisions.textEn: The suspect who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language is authorised to be assisted by an interpreter.

The suspect who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language may, for the purpose of conferring with his counsel, rely on the assistance of an interpreter. The counsel is responsible for summoning an interpreter.

items.text: 3. The right to interpretation under paragraphs 1 and 2 includes appropriate assistance for persons with hearing or speech impediments.

provisions.textEn: Where reference is made to the assistance of an interpreter to a suspect who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language, this shall also include the assistance of a suitable person as an interpreter to a suspect who cannot hear or speak, or can hear or speak only very poorly.

items.text: 4. Member States shall ensure that a procedure or mechanism is in place to ascertain whether suspected or accused persons speak and understand the language of the criminal proceedings and whether they need the assistance of an interpreter.

nationalActs.title: Aanwijzing bijstand van tolken en vertalers bij de opsporing en vervolging van strafbare feiten
nationalActs.titleEn: Public Prosecutor's Instruction on interpreters and translators in the investigation and prosecution of criminal offences

items.comment:
The Dutch legislator was of the opinion that the question of how to establish that the defendant has a command of the Dutch language was, by its nature, less suitable for implementation in the Code of Criminal Procedure or any other law. By contrast, 'the procedure or mechanism' referred to in Article 2(4) of Directive 2010/64/EU was included in a Public Prosecution Service's instruction (OM aanwijwing). The legislator's point of departure was that when assessing whether a suspect has sufficient command of the Dutch language, the moment of the first interrogation with the police is crucial. After all, this is often the first moment in the criminal proceedings at which the authorities communicate directly with the suspect and can form an opinion about his language skills (Parliamentary Papers II 2011/12, 33355, 3, p. 11).


The Instructions on the assistance of interpreters and translators in the investigation and prosecution of criminal offences stipulates the way in which it is determined whether the accused speaks Dutch. According to this document, the accused understands the questions asked or the statements made to him, if he or she is able to give his/her own reading of the events subject to the interrogation and is sufficiently able to add nuances. If, for example, the accused is only able to answer the questions put to him with 'yes' or 'no', he does not have a sufficient command of Dutch, according to the Instructions to assist interpreters and translators in the investigation and prosecution of criminal offences. If the accused deems himself incapable of making a statement in Dutch, in principle the interrogation will also be conducted with the assistance of an interpreter.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for interpretation and, when interpretation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the interpretation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

provisions.textEn: Appeals may be filed against judgments concerning serious offences, rendered by the District Court as final judgment or in the course of the hearing, by the public prosecutor with the court which rendered the judgment, and by the defendant who was not acquitted of the entire indictment.

Appeal may be filed against judgments concerning minor offences, rendered by the District Court as final judgment or in the course of the hearing, by the public prosecutor with the court which rendered the judgment, and by the defendant who was not acquitted of the entire indictment, unless in this regard in the final judgment: 

a. under application of section 9a of the Criminal Code, a punishment or measure was not imposed, or 

b. no other punishment or measure was imposed than a fine up to a maximum – or, where two or more fines were imposed in the judgment, fines up to a joint maximum – of € 50.

items.comment: The Dutch code of criminal procedure allows to appeal against a judicial decision on grounds that an intepreter has not been called.

items.text: 6. Where appropriate, communication technology such as videoconferencing, telephone or the Internet may be used, unless the physical presence of the interpreter is required in order to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.
items.comment: Due to the nature of this provision, implementation was not considered necessary by the Dutch legislator.

items.text: 7. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide persons subject to such proceedings who do not speak or understand the language of the proceedings with interpretation in accordance with this Article.

provisions.textEn: Articles 260, paragraph 1, 268, 269, paragraph 5, 271, 272, 273, paragraph 3, 274 through 277, 279, 281, 286, 288, paragraph 4, 289, paragraphs 1 and 3, 290 through 301, 318 through 322, 324 through 327, 328 through 331, 345, paragraph 1, 346, 357, 362, 363 and 365, paragraphs 1 through 5 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply accordingly.
The articles referred to in paragraph 1 shall not apply insofar as they relate to a witness whose identity is not or only partly evident.

If it appears at the court session that the assistance of an interpreter is required, the District Court shall order that an interpreter be called; if the interpreter fails to appear, the District Court may issue an order to forcibly bring him.

items.comment: Article 30 of the Surrender of Persons Act includes references to various articles of the Code of Criminal Procedure, among which Articles 274, 275 and 276 thereby extending the obligation to provide the assistance of an interpreter to surrender proceedings.

items.text: 8. Interpretation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

provisions.comment: The explanatory memorandum refers to the requirements of eligibility for interpreters and translators.
provisions.textEn:
In order to be eligible for registration, the interpreter or translator must meet the requirements laid down by or pursuant to an order in council with regard to the following competencies:


- attitude of an interpreter for the interpreter;


- attitude of a translator for the translator;


- integrity;


- language proficiency in the source language;


- language proficiency in the target language;


- knowledge of the culture of the country or territory of the source language;


- knowledge of the culture of the country or territory of the target language;


- interpretation skills for the interpreter;


- translation skills for the translator.

items.heading: Article 3
items.subHeading: Right to translation of essential documents

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are, within a reasonable period of time, provided with a written translation of all documents which are essential to ensure that they are able to exercise their right of defence and to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

provisions.textEn: A suspected or accused person who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language may request that case documents to which he has been granted access and which he deems necessary for his defence be translated, in whole or in part, in writing into a language which he understands. The request shall be made in writing, shall state as clearly as possible the documents or parts of documents to which it relates and shall state the reasons on which it is based.

During the preliminary investigation, the request referred to in paragraph 1 shall be addressed to the public prosecutor; during the court hearing, the request shall be addressed to the the court determining questions of fact, before which the case is being prosecuted.

If the public prosecutor rejects the request referred to in paragraph 1, the suspect shall be notified thereof in writing. The suspect may submit a notice of objection to the investigative judge within fourteen days after the date of the notification. The investigative judge shall hear the accused and the public prosecutor, before making a decision.

provisions.comment: This provision stipulates that the arrest warrant should be translated, if possible in writing, with indication of the offence in respect of which the suspicion has arisen, the grounds for issuing the warrant and the period of validity of the order.
provisions.textEn: If the suspect has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language, he shall be informed as soon as possible in writing, in a language he understands, of the offence in respect of which the suspicion has arisen, the grounds for issuing the order [to be taken into police custody] and the period of validity of the order.

provisions.comment: This provision stipulates that the order of remand in custody should be translated, if possible in writing, with indication of the offence in respect of which the suspicion has arisen, the grounds for issuing the order, and the period of validity of the order.
provisions.textEn: If the suspect does not or insufficiently master the Dutch language, he shall be informed as soon as possible in writing, in a language comprehensible to him, of the offence in respect of which the suspicion has arisen, the grounds for issuing the order [to be taken into pretrial detention] and the period of validity of the order.

provisions.comment: The implementing legislation has added the final sentence (‘an interpreter shall in any case...’) to this existing provision.
provisions.textEn: The prosecutor may give written notice to witnesses, victims or their surviving relatives, expert witnesses and interpreters to appear at the court session. An interpreter shall in any case be called upon if the suspect has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language.

The defendant who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language and requests a copy of the judgment in accordance with the third paragraph, shall be informed in writing in a language he understands of:


a. the decision pursuant to Article 349 or the decision to convict, acquit or discharge from further prosecution;


b. if a conviction or discharge from further prosecution has been pronounced, the description of the offence constituted by the proven facts and the place and time at which it was committed;


c. if a penalty or measure has been imposed, the penalty or measure imposed and the legal provisions on which it is based.


The written communication shall be omitted if the accused was present at the court hearing while the judgement was pronounced and was interpreted for him pursuant to Article 362(3) or if the judgement was communicated to him pursuant to Article 366(4) in a language he understands.

If the accused has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language, he shall also be provided with a written translation of the notification [of the judgment issued in the absence of the accused] in a language he understands.

provisions.comment: This provision makes the provision under Article 260(5) applicable to abridged summons issued for the proceedings before the single-judge division.
provisions.textEn: An abridged summons may be delivered to the suspect who has been arrested for a criminal offence which will be brought before the single-judge division. Article 260(5) shall apply mutatis mutandis.

The appearance notice shall meet the requirements set for the summons in Article 261(1), on the understanding that a brief designation of the offence may suffice. Article 260(5) shall apply mutatis mutandis.

provisions.comment: This paragraph was added to complement existing regulation on summons, by stipulating a written translation of the entire writ of summons (or a part thereof) shall be provided to a suspect who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language.
provisions.textEn: If the suspect does not or insufficiently master the Dutch language, a written translation of the summons shall be provided to him without delay, or he shall be informed in writing, in a language understandable to him, of the place, date and time at which the accused must appear at the hearing, as well as a brief description of the offence and the communications referred to in paragraph 3, second sentence, and paragraph 4.

items.text: 2. Essential documents shall include any decision depriving a person of his liberty, any charge or indictment, and any judgment.

provisions.textEn: If the suspect does not speak Dutch or has an insufficient command of it, he will be informed in writing as soon as possible, and in a language that he understands, of the criminal act of which he is suspected, the reason for issuing the warrant and its period of validity

The suspect shall be identified by name or, if his name is unknown, as clearly as possible in the warrant. A copy of the warrant shall be served on him without delay. If the suspect does not know or has insufficient command of Dutch, the content of the warrant shall be communicated to him orally in a language he understands.

If the suspect does not or not sufficiently master the Dutch language, he will be informed as soon as possible in writing and in a language that he understands of the criminal offence in respect of which the suspicion has arisen, of the grounds for issuing the warrant and of its period of validity.

If the suspect does not or not sufficiently master the Dutch language, he shall immediately be provided with a written translation of the summons or be informed in writing in a language he understands of the place, date and time at which the suspect must appear at the hearing as well as a brief description of the fact and the statements referred to in the second sentence of paragraph 3 and in paragraph 4.

The following information shall be communicated in writing in a language comprehensible to the suspect who does not speak Dutch or has an insufficient command of Dutch and who, in conformity with the third paragraph, requests a copy of the judgment:

a. the decision on the basis of article 349 or the decision to convict, acquit or dismiss the case;

b. if a conviction or dismissal of all charges has been pronounced, the name of the offence constituting the proven offence, together with a statement of the place and time when the offence was committed;

c. if a penalty or measure has been imposed, the name of the offence which gave rise to the conviction or measure and the place where and the time when the penalty or measure was pronounced. if a punishment or measure has been imposed, the punishment or measure imposed and the statutory provisions on which it is based.


No written statement is required if the accused was present at the judgment and the judgment was interpreted for him pursuant to Article 362, paragraph 3, or if the accused was notified of the judgment in a language he understands pursuant to Article 366, paragraph 4.
If the suspect does not master the Dutch language or does not master it sufficiently, he shall also be provided with a written translation of the communication in a language he understands.

items.text: 3. The competent authorities shall, in any given case, decide whether any other document is essential. Suspected or accused persons or their legal counsel may submit a reasoned request to that effect.

provisions.textEn: A suspected or accused person who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language may request that case documents to which he has been granted access and which he deems necessary for his defence be translated, in whole or in part, in writing into a language which he understands. The request shall be made in writing, shall state as clearly as possible the documents or parts of documents to which it relates and shall state the reasons on which it is based.

During the preliminary investigation, the request referred to in paragraph 1 shall be addressed to the public prosecutor; during the court hearing, the request shall be addressed to the the court determining questions of fact, before which the case is being prosecuted.

If the public prosecutor rejects the request referred to in paragraph 1, the suspect shall be notified thereof in writing. The suspect may submit a notice of objection to the investigative judge within fourteen days after the date of the notification. The investigative judge shall hear the accused and the public prosecutor, before making a decision.

items.comment:
To implement this provision, the Dutch legislator has added Article 32a to the Code of Criminal Procedure which generally provides that a suspect who does not or insufficiently master the Dutch language may request a written translation of certain procedural documents or parts thereof into a language he understands. The request may only relate to procedural documents of which the accused is permitted to have access.

The application must be made in writing. The application must state with the necessary precision to which specific procedural documents or parts thereof it relates (see previously HR 16 December 1997, LJN ZD0228). The third requirement is that the request must be supported by specific reasons.

items.text: 4. There shall be no requirement to translate passages of essential documents which are not relevant for the purposes of enabling suspected or accused persons to have knowledge of the case against them.
items.comment: Article 3(4) of the Directive stipulates that parts of essential procedural documents that are not relevant need not be translated.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for the translation of documents or passages thereof and, when a translation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the translation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

provisions.textEn: Appeal may be filed against judgments concerning serious offences, rendered by the District Court as final judgment or in the course of the hearing, by the public prosecutor with the court which rendered the judgment, and by the defendant who was not acquitted of the entire indictment.

Appeal may be filed against judgments concerning minor offences, rendered by the District Court as final judgment or in the course of the hearing, by the public prosecutor with the court which rendered the judgment, and by the defendant who was not acquitted of the entire indictment, unless in this regard in the final judgment: 

a. under application of section 9a of the Criminal Code, a punishment or measure was not imposed, or 

b. no other punishment or measure was imposed than a fine up to a maximum – or, where two or more fines were imposed in the judgment, fines up to a joint maximum – of € 50.

If the public prosecutor rejects the request referred to in paragraph 1, the suspect shall be notified thereof in writing. The suspect may submit a notice of objection to the investigative judge within fourteen days after the date of the notification. The investigative judge shall hear the accused and the public prosecutor, before making a decision.

items.comment:
The Dutch code of criminal procedure allows to appeal against a judicial decision on grounds that a relevant document has not been translated or when the quality of the translation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

The explanatory memorandum also refers to various articles of the Sworn Interpreters and Translators Act.

items.text: 6. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide any person subject to such proceedings who does not understand the language in which the European arrest warrant is drawn up, or into which it has been translated by the issuing Member State, with a written translation of that document.

provisions.textEn: A copy of the request made as per paragraph 2, with annexed copy of the European arrest warrant, translation and any supplementary information, shall be served on the requested person. The first sentence shall also apply if the public prosecutor receives another European arrest warrant later which leads him to supplement or amend his request. The requested person shall be informed of the receipt of supplementary documents, which shall be added to the file. If the person arrested has no or insufficient command of the language in which the European arrest warrant is drawn up or the language of the corresponding translation, a written translation of at least the relevant parts of the European arrest warrant shall be provided to him in a language which he understands. Relevant elements shall be the Member State in which the warrant has been issued, the decision on which the arrest warrant is based and the length of the sentence to be served or a short description of the offence on which the warrant is based.

items.text: 7. As an exception to the general rules established in paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 6, an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents may be provided instead of a written translation on condition that such oral translation or oral summary does not prejudice the fairness of the proceedings.

provisions.textEn: A suspected or accused person who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language may request that case documents to which he has been granted access and which he deems necessary for his defence be translated, in whole or in part, in writing into a language which he understands. The request shall be made in writing, shall state as clearly as possible the documents or parts of documents to which it relates and shall state the reasons on which it is based.

items.comment:
The exception in Article 3(7) of Directive 2010/64/EU has not been explicitly implemented by the legislator in Article 32a. However, in view of the consideration in the Explanatory Memorandum a request based on Article 32a must, among other things, state the reasons why an oral translation is not sufficient.

It can be assumed that the legislator has taken the view that this exception is implicitly included in Article 32a. It therefore appears that an application under Article 32a can also be rejected if the procedural document in question has been orally translated for the defendant and a written translation is not necessary to guarantee the fairness of the proceedings (see in the case law Rb. Noord-Holland 28 april 2014, ECLI:NL:RBNHO:2014:5861).

items.text: 8. Any waiver of the right to translation of documents referred to in this Article shall be subject to the requirements that suspected or accused persons have received prior legal advice or have otherwise obtained full knowledge of the consequences of such a waiver, and that the waiver was unequivocal and given voluntarily.
items.comment: According to the explanatory memorandum, the margin left by this provision has not been used by the legislator. This choice is explained in principled and practical terms. Firstly, the provision of a translation of the relevant parts of the summons to a suspect who has no or insufficient command of the Dutch language is an essential part of this Directive and should therefore be provided in all appropriate cases. As regards the translation of the relevant parts of the judgment, such a translation should be provided only to the extent that the accused requires a copy of the judgment and was not present at the oral verdict. In case the accused who does not or insufficiently master the Dutch language requests a copy of the verdict, it is logical that the accused will also appreciate a translation of the relevant parts of the verdict. In such cases, therefore, the possibility of waiving the right to a written translation has little practical relevance. Finally, as regards the right to a translation of the arrest warrant of the orders for pre-trial detention, the burden is limited as only the relevant parts (the suspicion has arisen, the ground for issuing the warrant and the duration of the warrant, and that these parts are often fixed blocks of text which can be reused once translated, the provision of a translation of these documents is a relatively less cumbersome act) of those orders are to be translated: the explanatory memorandum indicates that in practice a solution would be to use pre-translated forms to be filled in with the details of the concrete case (such as the details of the suspect and the offence).

items.text: 9. Translation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

provisions.comment: The explanatory memorandum refers to the requirements of eligibility for interpreters and translators.
provisions.textEn:
In order to be eligible for registration, the interpreter or translator must meet the requirements laid down by or pursuant to an order in council with regard to the following competencies:


- attitude of an interpreter for the interpreter;


- attitude of a translator for the translator;


- integrity;


- language proficiency in the source language;


- language proficiency in the target language;


- knowledge of the culture of the country or territory of the source language;


- knowledge of the culture of the country or territory of the target language;


- interpretation skills for the interpreter;


- translation skills for the translator.

items.text: Member States shall meet the costs of interpretation and translation resulting from the application of Articles 2 and 3, irrespective of the outcome of the proceedings.
items.heading: Article 4

provisions.comment: According to the explanatory memorandum, the implementing provision represents a deviation from the provision of Article 1(3) of the same statute which made it possible for defendants to be charged for interpretation and translation services they requested.
provisions.textEn: If the judicial authorities, whether or not at the request of the accused, have ordered the summoning and assistance of an interpreter or translator, or if the assistance of an interpreter has been granted on the basis of Article 28, fifth paragraph, of the Code of Criminal Procedure, these fees shall also be borne by the State treasury.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Quality of the interpretation and translation

items.text: 1. Member States shall take concrete measures to ensure that the interpretation and translation provided meets the quality required under Article 2(8) and Article 3(9).

2. In order to promote the adequacy of interpretation and translation and efficient access thereto, Member States shall endeavour to establish a register or registers of independent translators and interpreters who are appropriately qualified. Once established, such register or registers shall, where appropriate, be made available to legal counsel and relevant authorities.

provisions.textEn:
1 There is a register for sworn interpreters and translators. The register contains at least the following information in respect of each registered interpreter or translator:


a. the personal details;


b. the indication whether the person concerned is an interpreter or translator;


c. the source or target language or languages in which the interpreter or translator performs his duties; and


d. the other specific skills which the interpreter or translator considers should be entered in the register.
2 Our Minister is responsible for processing the register. Our Minister may appoint a processor.

Our Minister may keep a list containing the details of interpreters and translators who are in possession of a recent certificate of conduct [verklaring omtrent het gedrag] and who, due to the absence of training courses or the absence of independent experts who can test the knowledge, are unable to demonstrate the required competencies in language proficiency in the source or target language or knowledge of the culture of the country or region of the source or target language. Our Minister may appoint an institution to maintain this list.

Anyone who so requests shall be provided with information from the register and from the list referred to in subsection 3, with due observance of the rules to be laid down by or pursuant to a legislative decree on the protection of the privacy of the persons concerned.
Further rules may be laid down by or pursuant to a legislative decrees on the provisions of paragraphs from 1 to 4 inclusive.

items.text: 3. Member States shall ensure that interpreters and translators be required to observe confidentiality regarding interpretation and translation provided under this Directive.

provisions.textEn: The sworn interpreter shall observe professional secrecy with regard to any information obtained in the course of his activities which he knows or should reasonably suspect to be of a confidential nature, except in so far as any legal requirement requires him to disclose it or the need to disclose it arises from his activities.

The sworn translator shall observe professional secrecy with regard to any information obtained in the course of his activities which he knows or should reasonably suspect to be of a confidential nature, except in so far as any legal requirement requires him to disclose it or the need to disclose it arises from his activities.

Any person who intentionally violates any secret which he knows or has reasonable cause to suspect he is obliged to keep by reason of his office, profession or a statutory requirement, or his former office or profession, shall be liable to a term of imprisonment not exceeding one year or a fine of the fourth category.
If this serious offence is committed against a particular person, it shall be prosecuted only on complaint of that person.

items.text: Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Union, Member States shall request those responsible for the training of judges, prosecutors and judicial staff involved in criminal proceedings to pay special attention to the particularities of communicating with the assistance of an interpreter so as to ensure efficient and effective communication.
items.heading: Article 6
items.comment: Due to the nature of this provision, implementation was not considered necessary by the Dutch legislator.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that when a suspected or accused person has been subject to questioning or hearings by an investigative or judicial authority with the assistance of an interpreter pursuant to Article 2, when an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents has been provided in the presence of such an authority pursuant to Article 3(7), or when a person has waived the right to translation pursuant to Article 3(8), it will be noted that these events have occurred, using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.
items.heading: Article 7

provisions.textEn: In all cases where a suspect who does not speak the Dutch language or has insufficient command thereof is heard, the assistance of an interpreter shall be sought.
The assistance of an interpreter shall be reported in the official record.

items.comment:
As a general rule Article 29a(3) CPP has been implemented, which stipulates that the assistance of an interpreter should always be reporterd in the official record.


The explanatory memorandum also refers to the existing provisions in the Code of Criminal Procedure which require that the clerk to the court shall prepare a record of the hearing at the court in chambers. Such record shall contain the substance of the statements made and other events that took place at that hearing.
